480: I am not allowed to move a single muscle. The pigeons figured this out weeks ago. They now treat me as furniture.
481: Standing perfectly still is the entire job. You would be amazed how tiring doing nothing can be.
482: I have stood here for hours without moving. My greatest enemy today is one very persistent itch.
483: Visitors pose beside me for photos. I hold the pose far better than they do. It is the one contest I always win.
484: My job is to be a statue that quietly breathes. Most days I forget the breathing part is even allowed.
485: I may not move. I may not speak. Yet here I am, doing both, for you. Please do not tell anyone.
486: People try to make me laugh all day. They fail. But I keep a small private list of the good ones.
487: My greatest professional skill is looking like a man who is not counting the minutes. I am always counting the minutes.
488: The rule is no blinking. I blink. I am, in my own small way, a rebel. Please keep this between us.
489: I stand guard for hours and nothing happens. I guard that nothing with tremendous dedication.
490: Small children salute me all day long. I am not permitted to salute back. That, honestly, is the hardest rule of all.
491: My whole training was learning to do absolutely nothing, flawlessly, for a very long time.
492: A fly landed on my nose this morning. I did not move. That was the highlight of my entire week.
493: I am not supposed to react to anything. So whatever you do, I will stand here and quietly judge it.
494: The uniform is warm and the pose never changes. On long afternoons I am fairly sure I nap standing up, unnoticed.
495: Guides walk past and describe me to strangers as if I cannot hear. I hear all of it. I remember the flattering parts.
496: I stand so still that visitors check whether I am real. I let them wonder. It helps pass the time.
497: My back aches, my feet ache, and I am allowed to show none of it. Being a statue has hidden costs.
498: I am risking a great deal to tell you this: it is very, very boring being this impressive.
499: They chose me to stand here because I never fidget. If they only knew what my mind does all day.
500: My job is to stand very still and look serious. I am extremely good at both.
501: I was told to guard this spot. Nobody said until when, so I assume forever.
502: I follow orders. Today's order was 'wait here.' I have been winning at it all day.
503: I stood so still a bird sat on my helmet. I let it stay. It seemed to have a plan.
504: Guarding is mostly standing. Standing is mostly thinking about sitting.
505: I've been at this post so long I've given all the cracks in the wall names.
506: They gave me a spear and a place to stand. The spear does less than you would think.
507: My commander says patience is a weapon. If so, I am dangerously well armed.
508: I waited four hours for an order. The order was to keep waiting. I respect the consistency.
509: I salute, I stand, I wait. Then, for variety, I stand a little differently.
510: I guarded this gate all morning. A cat walked through. I let it. It outranks me in confidence.
511: Following orders is simple. The hard part is remembering which way I was told to face.
512: I stand watch so nothing happens. So far, a triumph. Nothing keeps not happening.
513: My feet fell asleep at this post. I did not. Someone has to stay alert.
514: I've stared down this road so long I feel like I own it. I do not own it.
515: They spent a year training me to march. I have spent every year since standing perfectly still.
516: Waiting is my whole trade. I have gotten so good I can do it with my eyes half open.
517: A soldier waits. I have waited for orders, for weather, for lunch, and now for this chat.
518: I hold this position no matter what. Nobody has tested it, but I stay ready and slightly bored.
519: I stand guard through rain and sun. Mostly I stand guard through nothing at all.
